title: How Does Thread Depth Influence the Mechanical Strength of Dental Implants?
text: This investigation focused on analyzing the influence of thread depth on the mechanical strength of dental implants in a controlled laboratory environment. A total of 60 titanium dental implants with varying thread depths (0.5 mm, 1.0 mm, and 1.5 mm) were embedded into synthetic bone models simulating medium density bone (0.25 g/cm(3)). The implants were subjected to axial loading using a servo-hydraulic testing machine, with measurements taken to determine the failure load and stiffness. Data were analyzed using ANOVA, with a significance threshold set at P<0.05. The findings indicated that implants with a thread depth of 1.5 mm exhibited significantly higher mean failure loads compared to those with 0.5 mm (P<0.01) and 1.0 mm (P<0.05). Stiffness values were also highest in the 1.5 mm thread depth group, showing a statistically significant difference from the 0.5 mm group (P<0.01). The study's results suggest that variations in thread depth may play an important role in the mechanical performance of dental implants.

title: How Does Thread Depth Influence the Mechanical Strength of Dental Implants?
text: This investigation sought to determine the impact of varying thread depths on the mechanical stability of dental implants in standard bone conditions. A total of 60 titanium implants with thread depths of 0.5 mm, 1.0 mm, and 1.5 mm were inserted into synthetic bone blocks simulating average human bone density. The insertion torque was measured using a calibrated torque wrench, and mechanical stability was assessed through pull-out tests conducted with a universal testing machine. Data were analyzed using ANOVA, revealing significant differences in insertion torque among the groups (F(2,57) = 8.34, p < .001). The mean insertion torque values were 25.4 Ncm for the 0.5 mm group, 35.6 Ncm for the 1.0 mm group, and 45.2 Ncm for the 1.5 mm group. Additionally, the pull-out strength demonstrated a notable increase with deeper threads, with average values of 152.3 N for the 0.5 mm, 195.4 N for the 1.0 mm, and 238.7 N for the 1.5 mm implants (p < .01). These findings suggest a correlation between thread depth and mechanical stability.
